heroHeadline: Tennessee Grants First US Fusion License to Type One Energy; Pacific Fusion Breaks Ground on $1B NM Campus; Kyoto Fusioneering Raises $162M
heroSubtitle: A landmark week for fusion infrastructure and regulation. On August 31, Tennessee's environmental regulator issued the nation's first fusion-specific commercial license, clearing Type One Energy to begin building its Infinity One stellarator prototype at TVA's Bull Run Energy Complex ahead of a planned 400 MWe pilot plant targeting 2034 startup. On August 26, Pacific Fusion broke ground on a $1 billion research and manufacturing campus at Mesa del Sol in Albuquerque, New Mexico, pairing the milestone with a new DOE/NNSA memorandum of understanding on high-yield fusion and pulsed-power technology; the site will house a Demonstration System targeting net facility gain by 2030. On August 24, Japan's Kyoto Fusioneering closed a ¥25.72 billion (~$162M) Series D — backed by a Korea-Japan investor consortium including Posco and Doosan — to scale its UNITY tritium fuel-cycle programme across facilities in Japan, Canada, and Tennessee. Global private fusion investment remains above $15 billion following July's record CFS and Helion rounds.
